script: inline diagnostic recorded from the /code session (see provenance/wp3_band_tension_diagnostic_execution.json for the parent analysis)
issue: #1d — is the anchor prior or the photometry the unreliable side for CygOB2-B?
test: Correlate (prior mean - photometry-only A_V) against each star's 8th-nearest-anchor separation, within each subgroup so any subgroup-level offset is removed.  Anchor separation is a property of sky position and carries no photometric information, so a correlation implicates the PRIOR rather than the photometry.
finding: The disagreement grows with anchor distance ONLY in CygOB2-B (rho=+0.421, p=1.2e-18); CygOB2-A is slightly negative (-0.131) and CygOB2-C is consistent with zero (-0.083, p=0.10).  Since anchor separation is independent of the photometry, this implicates the prior as the unreliable side for B specifically.
caveat: Still does not prove the prior causes B's WP5 tilt: CygOB2-A carries a comparable absolute prior pull (+0.415 mag) and passes the gate.
